value.overview: The Pale-vented Pigeon (Patagioenas cayennensis) is a large, mainly dull purple-gray pigeon of the tropical Americas. It is associated with forest edges, river corridors, open woodland, plantations, pastures with scattered trees, and other partly open habitats. Unlike many forest pigeons, it often flies and forages in relatively open country. In Costa Rica it is a resident species, especially in humid lowlands and foothills on both the Caribbean and Pacific slopes.
value.classification: The Pale-vented Pigeon belongs to the pigeon and dove family Columbidae and the New World pigeon genus Patagioenas. Its scientific name is Patagioenas cayennensis.
value.identification: This large pigeon has a gray head, pale throat, pinkish or purplish-brown body, dark wings, a gray tail, and a distinctly pale whitish belly and undertail area. The bill is black. Some birds show a subtle coppery or greenish gloss on the neck. It can be confused with the Red-billed Pigeon, but the Pale-vented Pigeon has a black bill and a paler vent, while the Red-billed Pigeon is generally darker and has a reddish bill. Its call begins with a deep coo followed by repeated three-note phrases.
value.rangeHabitat: The species ranges from southern Mexico through Central America and across much of northern and central South America. In Costa Rica it occurs on both Caribbean and Pacific slopes, mainly in humid lowlands and adjacent foothills, with records from areas such as the Sarapiquí and Tortuguero regions, Caño Negro, the southern Pacific lowlands, and the Central Pacific. It favors forest edges, riverbanks, mangroves, marshy areas, plantations, second-growth vegetation, and pastures or savannas containing large trees. It is less typical of extensive, unbroken mature forest.
value.migrationStatus: Generally resident throughout its range, including Costa Rica. It is not considered a regular long-distance migrant, although local movements may follow fruit availability and water sources.
value.breeding: The Pale-vented Pigeon usually places a simple, rather flimsy platform of twigs in a shrub or small tree, often in dense vegetation, a palm, pasture thicket, savanna, or open woodland. A clutch normally consists of one white egg. Breeding behavior includes a display flight in which the bird glides in a semicircle back toward its perch. Detailed information on nesting seasons and success is uneven across the range, including Costa Rica.
value.dietFeeding: It feeds mainly on fruits, berries, and seeds, often taking small fruits from trees and shrubs. Reported food plants include members of the melastome, nightshade, and other fruit-producing groups. Birds commonly forage high in the canopy or along forest edges, but may also feed in more open areas. Individuals are often seen alone or in pairs, while small groups can gather at fruiting trees, drinking sites, or favored perches.
value.behavior: The Pale-vented Pigeon is usually solitary or found in small groups. It often perches quietly on high branches and makes a fast, direct flight with strong wingbeats. Males perform a display involving a curved or semicircular glide from a perch. Birds may become conspicuous when calling from exposed treetops, crossing clearings, or visiting fruiting trees. In Costa Rica, it is most likely to be encountered along forest margins, rivers, wetlands, and open lowland habitats with scattered trees.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not clearly quantified, but the species remains widespread and is generally considered common in suitable habitat.
